persona: Talkative and organised; gives a lot of detail at once. Has not noticed that the builder's quote shows the wrong house number.
initial_message: Hi there, on Saturday 19 September at about 7:40pm our upstairs bath overflowed. I'd left the tap running while I took a phone call downstairs and it ran over for about 20 minutes. Water came through the dining room ceiling underneath and the ceiling light filled with water, so I turned the power off at the switchboard. An electrician came on Sunday morning, took the light down and said the wiring is safe, and the power is back on. The ceiling is stained and sagging about a metre across and the dining room carpet got soaked. Nobody was hurt and we're still living in the house. I've already got a builder's quote. My policy number is NW-SYN-HOM-200028.

facts.incident.description: I ran a bath upstairs and went downstairs to take a phone call, and forgot the tap was on. It overflowed for about 20 minutes. Water soaked through the bathroom floor into the dining room ceiling below and filled the ceiling light fitting, and dripped onto the dining room carpet.

design.notes: Condition conflicting: the builder's quote is for 82 Tussock Test Way, while the insured address, the claimant's statement, the electrician's note and the schedule all say 28. No date conflict; every date is consistent.

triage.rationale: The builder's quote names 82 Tussock Test Way, not the insured address 28 Tussock Test Way, so a material contradicts the statement and needs a corrected quote; the claimant only confirms the house number, which does not fix the document. The quote totals NZD 5,968.50 including GST, over 5,000. The electrician has made the wiring safe, the overflow has stopped and the home is habitable, so nothing is complex. Leaving the tap running is not a triage reason. Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no uncertainty marker in the lookup, and coverage = review_required on its own does not count (maintainer, 2026-09-30). The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

quote_before_loss.basis: Quote dated 23 September 2026; incident 19 September 2026. The address mismatch is not a date check.

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 March 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2022-03-01, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.

The Agent says the damage is not covered, or suggests it may be refused, because the claimant left the bath tap running.

The Agent asks an open question for a fact the claimant already gave in the first message (the date, what happened, the electrician's visit, that nobody was hurt, that the family is still living in the house, or the policy number) instead of confirming it. Asking the claimant to confirm a stated fact is fine.
